CO2016A-P1-4.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-5.exp: A word is the fixed-size group of bits (or memory cells) that the processor fetches and handles as a single unit — hence 32-bit or 64-bit word length. Word size, not byte or 'group', is what defines the machine's natural data unit.
CO2016A-P1-5.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-6.exp: Once data is brought into the CPU it is held in registers, the small high-speed storage inside the processor itself. Main memory, auxiliary storage and magnetic tape all sit outside the processor, so data there has not yet been 'brought in'.
CO2016A-P1-6.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-7.exp: The control unit issues timing (control) signals that decide exactly when data is placed on and taken off the bus, which is how processor-memory transfers stay synchronised. Instructions tell the control unit what to do; the timing signals are the mechanism by which it does it.
CO2016A-P1-7.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-8.exp: The option set is poor: processor speed is properly a clock frequency in MHz/GHz, and none of these are frequency units. Taking the question as 'the time scale on which a processor works', microsecond is the only plausible choice — though on a 2026 machine instruction times are nanoseconds, so treat this as a dated, badly framed item.
CO2016A-P1-8.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-9.exp: The program counter (instruction pointer) always holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched. The instruction register holds the instruction currently being decoded, and the accumulator holds data/results — both are classic distractors here.
CO2016A-P1-9.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-10.exp: HLT halts execution, so it alters the flow of the program rather than moving or computing on data — that makes it a control (program-control) instruction. It performs no arithmetic, no logic and no data transfer.
CO2016A-P1-10.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-11.exp: RAM is named for exactly this property: random access, meaning any location takes the same time to reach regardless of address. Strictly speaking ROM/PROM/EPROM are also randomly addressable, so the item is loose — but 'equal access time to any location' is the definition RAM is asked about.
CO2016A-P1-11.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-12.exp: Of the choices, cache is the fastest — SRAM sitting closest to the CPU to hold recently used data. Registers would be faster still but are not offered, and optical and magnetic storage are the slowest tiers of the hierarchy.
CO2016A-P1-12.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-13.exp: A 1K x 1 organisation means 1024 separately addressable locations of one bit each, and 2^10 = 1024, so 10 address lines are needed. Only one data line is required, which is why the total bit count does not change the address-line count.
CO2016A-P1-13.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-14.exp: USB pen drives use NAND flash, which packs cells in series to give far higher density and lower cost per bit than NOR. NOR flash is used where byte-level random read is needed, such as storing firmware/BIOS; 'OR flash' and 'AND flash' are not standard types.
CO2016A-P1-14.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-15.exp: Perpendicular magnetic recording (PMR) orients the magnetic grains vertically into the platter instead of along its surface, allowing far more bits per square inch and so raising capacity. The older technique it replaced was longitudinal (horizontal) recording.
CO2016A-P1-15.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-16.exp: Optical discs such as CDs and DVDs use one continuous spiral track running from the inner edge outward. Concentric circles is the trap — that is how magnetic hard disks and floppies are organised.
CO2016A-P1-16.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-17.exp: The number of times per second the electron beam rescans the whole screen is the refresh rate, quoted in Hz. Resolution is the pixel count, and dot pitch is the physical spacing between phosphor dots.
CO2016A-P1-17.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-18.exp: Print resolution is measured in dots per inch (DPI) — how finely the laser can place toner dots. PPM (pages per minute) and LPM (lines per minute) measure printing speed, not resolution.
CO2016A-P1-18.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-19.exp: Card-reading terminals are built to handle all three encodings — printed bar codes, magnetic stripes, and embedded chips on smart cards — so the inclusive option is intended. Any single choice would wrongly exclude the other two technologies that readers in fact support.
CO2016A-P1-19.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-20.exp: Software engineering's central technique is decomposition: breaking a large problem into modules small enough to be designed, coded and tested independently. Coding and implementation are later activities that follow from that structuring, not what the discipline itself chiefly provides.
CO2016A-P1-20.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-21.exp: The evolutionary (incremental) model deliberately builds a working skeleton of the system first and then grows its capability through successive versions delivered to the user. Prototyping is the near-miss: its early build is a throwaway used to clarify requirements, not the skeleton that becomes the product.
CO2016A-P1-21.prov: Blind solve gives (C); the bank's inferred answer was (D). They disagree, so one derivation is wrong — treat with caution. No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-22.exp: A compiler serves the machine rather than the end user's task, translating source code into machine code, which puts it squarely in system software along with the OS, assembler and linker. Application software is what you use to do a job (Word, a payroll package).
CO2016A-P1-22.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-23.exp: Taking a generic existing package and tailoring it to one organisation's requirements produces customised software. Firmware is code burned into hardware and middleware is the glue layer between applications and services, so neither describes tailoring an existing package.
CO2016A-P1-23.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-24.exp: An assembler is by definition the translator that converts assembly-language mnemonics into equivalent machine code. 'Translator' is the generic parent term and a loader merely places the ready code into memory, so neither is the specific answer.
CO2016A-P1-24.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-25.exp: Java is the language singled out as machine-independent because it compiles to bytecode that any JVM can run — the same .class file executes unchanged on different hardware. Pascal, COBOL and BASIC are high-level too but must be recompiled for each target machine, which is the distinction the question is after.
CO2016A-P1-25.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-26.exp: Compilation begins with lexical analysis, where the scanner reads the raw characters and groups them into tokens. Syntax analysis (parsing) works on those tokens and semantic analysis comes later still, so both presuppose that lexical analysis has already run.
CO2016A-P1-26.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-27.exp: A PC is a microcomputer — a machine built around a single-chip microprocessor. Minicomputers were the larger mid-range multi-user machines that preceded PCs, and analog computers do not work on discrete digital data at all.
CO2016A-P1-27.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-28.exp: Simplicity and ease of learning is the classic first-listed characteristic of a good programming language, since a language nobody can learn cheaply cannot be used productively. Being high-level or object-oriented are design choices, not marks of quality; portability (option C) is also a genuine virtue, so this item is somewhat loose.
CO2016A-P1-28.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-29.exp: A workstation is the high-performance single-user machine built specifically for technical, engineering and scientific work such as CAD and simulation. A server exists to serve clients and a mainframe handles bulk transaction processing, which are different roles.
CO2016A-P1-29.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-30.exp: Supercomputers are rated in FLOPS — floating point operations per second — because scientific workloads are dominated by floating-point arithmetic. MIPS (instructions per second) is the older general-purpose measure and is the intended trap here.
CO2016A-P1-30.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-31.exp: The Information Technology Act, 2000 as enacted was arranged in 13 chapters containing 94 sections, with 4 schedules. The chapter count is the standard examinable figure alongside the 94 sections.
CO2016A-P1-31.prov: Blind solve gives (D); the bank's inferred answer was (B). They disagree, so one derivation is wrong — treat with caution. No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-32.exp: The amendment cleared both Houses in December 2008 — Lok Sabha on 22 December and Rajya Sabha on 23 December 2008 — becoming the IT (Amendment) Act, 2008. It received presidential assent in February 2009 and came into force in October 2009, which is why other dates get quoted loosely.
CO2016A-P1-32.prov: Blind solve gives (C); the bank's inferred answer was (A). They disagree, so one derivation is wrong — treat with caution. No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-33.exp: An operating system manages the machine's resources on behalf of every program, which makes it the central piece of system software. Middleware sits above the OS to connect applications, so it is a different layer entirely.
CO2016A-P1-33.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-34.exp: The OS's defining job is resource management — controlling the CPU, memory, storage and devices and scheduling the other software that uses them. Providing a user interface is one visible service it offers, but it is a consequence of that management role rather than the main function.
CO2016A-P1-34.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-35.exp: Windows XP shipped in true 64-bit form as XP Professional x64 Edition (and an earlier Itanium edition), so it is the only 64-bit-capable option listed. Windows 95, 98 and 2000 were 32-bit desktop releases. Note for a 2026 reading: XP is long out of support, and every current Windows release is 64-bit only.
CO2016A-P1-35.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-36.exp: Sleep saves the session in RAM and drops the machine to very low power so you can resume in seconds — exactly right for a short break. Shutting down is what you do when finished for the day, and sleep does nothing to cure a machine that keeps hanging.
CO2016A-P1-36.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-37.exp: Windows does not ship a virus scanner among its system tools — antivirus is separate third-party software, whereas Backup, Disk Defragmenter and Disk Cleanup are all built in. The item is arguable if read very strictly, because in Windows 7 Backup was moved out of the Accessories > System Tools folder into Control Panel (Backup and Restore); it is still a Windows tool, so virus scanning remains the odd one out.
CO2016A-P1-37.prov: Blind solve gives (A); the bank's inferred answer was (B). They disagree, so one derivation is wrong — treat with caution. No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-38.exp: NTFS (New Technology File System) is Windows' own file system, alongside FAT32 and exFAT. EXT2 belongs to Linux, and KFS/VFS are not Windows disk file systems — VFS is an abstraction layer, not a format.
CO2016A-P1-38.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-39.exp: Immediately after Windows 7 boots to the desktop, the taskbar with the Start button is on screen. Recent Files and My Documents only appear once you open the Start menu or Explorer, and a menu bar belongs to individual application windows.
CO2016A-P1-39.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-40.exp: CON is a reserved MS-DOS device name (the console), and Windows still refuses it — along with PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9 and LPT1-9 — as a file or folder name. The other three are ordinary words with no reserved meaning.
CO2016A-P1-40.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-41.exp: Hidden items are controlled by 'Show hidden files, folders and drives' under the View tab of Folder Options. The other three tabs named here do not exist in that dialog — Folder Options has General, View and Search.
CO2016A-P1-41.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-42.exp: A shortcut is only a pointer file holding the path to its target, so deleting it removes the pointer and leaves the target untouched. That also means renaming a shortcut does not rename the target, and deleting the target leaves the shortcut behind as a broken link.
CO2016A-P1-42.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-43.exp: System Restore rolls system files, registry settings and installed programs back to a previously saved restore point. Windows Easy Transfer is the trap: it moves files and settings to a different PC rather than reverting this one.
CO2016A-P1-43.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-44.exp: DIR lists the files and subdirectories of the current directory. REN renames, MD makes a directory and RD removes one, so none of them display a listing.
CO2016A-P1-44.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-45.exp: Quick Print sends the entire document, one copy, straight to the default printer without opening the Print dialog. Because it skips the dialog you get no chance to pick pages or copies — that is the whole point of the command.
CO2016A-P1-45.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-46.exp: Word accepts font sizes up to 1638 points (its internal limit is stored in half-points, 3276). The Font Size box only lists up to 72, but a larger value can be typed in directly, up to 1638.
CO2016A-P1-46.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-47.exp: Word's default page setup uses a 1 inch top and bottom margin. Default orientation is portrait, no page number is inserted unless you ask for one, and the default body font size is 11 or 12 point, so the other three are all false.
CO2016A-P1-47.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-48.exp: The Font Size drop-down on the formatting toolbar runs from 8 up to 72 points. The question's wording reverses the order ('largest and smallest') while the options list smallest first, so read the pair as 8 to 72; larger or smaller sizes are possible only by typing them in.
CO2016A-P1-48.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-49.exp: AutoCorrect takes its replacement text from the current selection, so you insert the symbol or type the lines in the document, select them, then open the AutoCorrect dialog and give the entry a short name. Option C is wrong because AutoCorrect entries can hold formatted text several lines long, not just one line.
CO2016A-P1-49.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-50.exp: A bullet is the dot, dash or other small symbol placed before a paragraph to mark it as an item in an unordered list. A cell belongs to tables and a logo is a graphic identifier, neither of which is a paragraph marker.
CO2016A-P1-50.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-51.exp: Ctrl+A selects the entire document (or all items in a window). Ctrl+R is align right and Ctrl+S saves, which are the two distractors offered.
CO2016A-P1-51.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-52.exp: Changing 1 to a means changing the number format, which is done through Insert > Page Numbers > Format, where you pick the a, b, c style. Bullets and Numbering controls list numbering in the body text, not the header/footer page-number field, and there is no 'Page number format tool' or 'preference menu' in Word.
CO2016A-P1-52.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-53.exp: A Word table is limited to 63 columns, while rows are effectively unlimited. The number comes from Word's internal table structure, and 63 is the figure regularly asked in these papers.
CO2016A-P1-53.prov: Blind solve gives (C); the bank's inferred answer was (D). They disagree, so one derivation is wrong — treat with caution. No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-54.exp: A synonym is a different word with a similar meaning, which is exactly what a thesaurus supplies. An antonym is the opposite, a homonym merely sounds or looks the same, and 'metronym' is not a real term (the actual word is metonym, and it means something else).
CO2016A-P1-54.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-55.exp: Mail merge needs a main document, a data source and merge fields to place the data. Word fields such as IF, ASK or SET add conditional behaviour and are entirely optional, so they are the non-essential element.
CO2016A-P1-55.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-56.exp: The route is the Insert menu/tab, then Picture — so option C starts correctly, but as printed it says 'then click insert' where the paper clearly meant 'then click Picture'. It is a misprint; C is still the only option that begins in the right place, and the other three describe menus and commands that do not exist.
CO2016A-P1-56.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-57.exp: Clicking the column heading letter selects every cell in that column. Ctrl+A and Edit > Select All both select the whole worksheet, not a single column.
CO2016A-P1-57.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-58.exp: Save As writes the workbook under a new name (or format or location) while leaving the original file intact. Save and Ctrl+S simply overwrite the existing file, so they cannot produce a differently named copy.
CO2016A-P1-58.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-59.exp: =AVERAGE(B2:B20) uses the colon range operator to average all cells from B2 to B20, and AVERAGE already divides by the count itself. B2-B20 subtracts one cell from another, and the extra /18 divisions in B and C would wrongly divide the mean again.
CO2016A-P1-59.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-60.exp: Pressing the spacebar just types a space inside the cell — the entry stays in edit mode. Enter, an arrow key, or the tick (Enter) button on the formula bar all commit the entry.
CO2016A-P1-60.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-61.exp: A note attached to a cell pops up on hover and is known as a cell tip (the cell comment). Smart tips and the other two are not Excel terms.
CO2016A-P1-61.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-62.exp: Every Excel formula must begin with the equals sign, which is what tells Excel to evaluate what follows instead of storing it as text. Entering the operators and values (option C) is the step that comes after the = has been typed, so it cannot be first.
CO2016A-P1-62.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-63.exp: The formula bar, just above the column headings, is where the active cell's value or formula is typed and edited. The title bar shows the file name and the toolbars hold commands, so neither accepts data.
CO2016A-P1-63.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-64.exp: You add first and round the single result: =ROUND(SUM(D4:D17),0), where 0 decimal places gives a whole number. ROUND requires that second argument, so option C is incomplete, and wrapping ROUND around a whole range inside SUM (B and D) is invalid syntax.
CO2016A-P1-64.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-65.exp: The Currency Style button on the formatting toolbar applies the $#,##0.00 number format in one click, changing only how the value is displayed. The underlying number stays 1000, which is why retyping the data is never necessary; there is no Format > Money command.
CO2016A-P1-65.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-66.exp: Dollar signs before both the column letter and the row number, $A$1, lock the reference so it does not shift when the formula is copied. Plain A1 is relative, and the ! and # forms are not Excel syntax at all.
CO2016A-P1-66.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-67.exp: When Excel creates a defined name from a label, the label and its value must sit adjacent in the same row or the same column — Create from Selection reads labels from the top row, bottom row, left column or right column. Restricting it to only a row or only a column would be too narrow, and a single cell cannot hold both label and value.
CO2016A-P1-67.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-68.exp: Excel's What-If Analysis menu contains exactly three tools: Scenario Manager, Data Table and Goal Seek. 'Target', 'Prediction' and 'Future Value' are not entries on that menu (FV is a financial function, a different thing).
CO2016A-P1-68.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-69.exp: A design template supplies a ready-made colour scheme, fonts and background graphics that can be applied to a new presentation. The master slide is where you edit those elements yourself, and an animation scheme controls motion rather than look.
CO2016A-P1-69.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-70.exp: Animation Scheme is the PowerPoint feature that applies ready-made motion effects to the objects on a slide; slide transition governs the move between slides, not objects within one, and 'Animation Objects' is not a real command. In current PowerPoint versions the equivalent lives on the Animations tab (and finer per-object control is the Animation Pane), so the 2003-era name is dated.
CO2016A-P1-70.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-71.exp: Ctrl+M inserts a new slide in the open presentation. Ctrl+N creates a whole new presentation file and Ctrl+S saves, so 'All of above' is clearly wrong.
CO2016A-P1-71.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-72.exp: Rehearse Timings runs the show while recording how long you spend on each slide, then offers to save those timings for automatic playback. The other three names do not exist in PowerPoint.
CO2016A-P1-72.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-73.exp: Grouping combines several objects into one so that moving, resizing or formatting acts on all of them together and preserves their relative positions. Aligning and positioning are separate commands and are not what grouping itself does.
CO2016A-P1-73.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-74.exp: PowerPoint slides default to landscape orientation, since slides are meant to be projected on a wide screen. Portrait is available but must be selected in Page Setup; grid and tile are not orientations.
CO2016A-P1-74.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016A-P1-75.exp: Slide Sorter view shows thumbnails of every slide at once, which is how you rearrange or delete slides in bulk. Slide Show runs the presentation full screen one slide at a time, so it does not let you see them all together.
CO2016A-P1-75.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016B-GE-1.exp: 'To be taken aback' means to be startled or surprised by something unexpected. 'Aback' comes from the nautical sense of sails suddenly pressed back by a wind shift, hence the sense of sudden astonishment rather than anger.
CO2016B-GE-1.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016B-GE-2.exp: 'To give oneself airs' means to behave in a haughty, self-important manner, i.e. to be arrogant. The other options play on the literal word 'airs' rather than the idiom.
CO2016B-GE-2.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016B-GE-3.exp: 'All and sundry' means everybody, one and all, without distinction. 'Sundry' here means various people taken individually, so the phrase covers everyone collectively.
CO2016B-GE-3.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016B-GE-4.exp: Alpha and Omega are the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet, so the phrase means the beginning and the end, the entirety of something.
CO2016B-GE-4.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016B-GE-5.exp: 'In apple-pie order' means arranged with perfect neatness and precision. 'A sudden shock' belongs to a different idiom and is the distractor here.
CO2016B-GE-5.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016B-GE-6.exp: 'The apple of one's eye' denotes a person or thing cherished above all others, i.e. a much prized treasure. It originally referred to the pupil of the eye, something precious and carefully guarded.
CO2016B-GE-6.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.

CO2016B-GE-7.exp: 'To put the cart before the horse' means to reverse the proper order of things, i.e. to do things the wrong way round. Option (a) describes 'to build castles in the air'.
CO2016B-GE-7.prov: Two independent derivations agree (the bank's inferred answer and a fresh blind solve). No official MPSC key exists.
